new_laws.title: AN ACT TO PREVENT, DETER AND ELIMINATE ILLEGAL, UNREPORTED AND UNREGULATED FISHING, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8550, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE PHILIPPINE FISHERIES CODE OF 1998," AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
new_laws.summary: Amends the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 (RA 8550) to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to strengthen the conservation and management of Philippine fisheries and aquatic resources. Among its prohibited acts, it makes it unlawful to convert mangroves into fishponds or for any other purpose (Section 99), and to gather, possess, commercially transport, sell or export corals, or to commit any activity that damages coral reefs (Sections 96 and 97).
new_laws.note: Lapsed into law on 27 February 2015 without presidential signature (Art. VI, s.27(1), Constitution). Do not describe it as signed.

links.rationale: The Clean Air Act is the only listed statute that sets air-emission limits and penalises exceedance.
links.note: Stationary sources: §19 sets emission limits and §45 is the PAB daily fine. Motor vehicles are a separate track (§21, §46) and should be their own violation type. The criminal catch-all is §47 (₱10,000-₱100,000 and/or 6 months-6 years), which is not an administrative penalty.

links.rationale: §96 makes it unlawful to commit any activity that damages coral reefs; §97 bans muro-ami and other gear or methods destructive to coral.
links.note: No in-list statute covers coral damage generally. RA 7586 §20(e) (as amended by RA 11038) applies only inside NIPAS areas; RA 9275 §27(a) only where a discharge caused the damage.

links.rationale: RA 6969 is the dedicated hazardous-waste statute.
links.note: §13(d) covers storage, import and transit of hazardous and nuclear waste. §14(b) is the criminal penalty (12 years and 1 day to 20 years); §15 is administrative fines only (₱10,000-₱50,000). Citing §15 alone understates criminal liability.

links.rationale: §68 is the illegal-logging provision: cutting, gathering or removing timber or forest products from forest land without a licence, with confiscation of timber and equipment.
links.note: RA 7161 inserted the NIRC forest-charge sections as PD 705 §§68-77 and renumbered the old §§68-68-B, so confirm the number in a consolidated code. RA 11038 §20(c) applies inside protected areas; RA 9175 covers chainsaw possession/use.

links.rationale: §48(3) expressly prohibits the open burning of solid waste and §49(b) supplies the penalty; §3(kk) includes agricultural waste within solid waste.
links.note: RA 8749 §20 bans incineration of municipal/biomedical/hazardous waste but expressly exempts traditional small-scale siga and agricultural/cultural/health/food-preparation burning, so it is not the general hook. RA 9003 penalties are low (₱300-₱1,000), so LGUs often add ordinances.

links.rationale: §21(b) covers §20 paragraphs (f)-(n); the pairing is real but the type conflates occupancy and construction.
links.note: §20(n) is OCCUPANCY: 'occupying or dwelling in any public land within the protected area without clearance from the PAMB.' Construction or a business enterprise without clearance is §20(o) -> §21(c) (₱1,000,000-₱5,000,000 / 6-12 years). One 'intrusion' type cannot carry the right penalty for both; split the violation type or store the paragraph.

links.rationale: The violation type is dumping, not littering, so the open-dumping tier applies.
links.note: §48(9)/§49(d) is open dumping: ₱500,000 plus 5-10% of net annual income. The earlier mapping pointed at §48(1)/§49(a), which is the LITTERING tier (₱300-₱1,000 or 1-15 days community service) - a substantive understatement. Related: flood-prone burying §48(6)/§49(c); bulk dumping outside prescribed facilities §48(13)/§49(e).

links.rationale: §27(a) prohibits discharging material into a water body that causes pollution, and §27(i) prohibits discharging regulated pollutants without a valid permit; §28 fines ₱10,000-₱200,000 per day.
links.note: PD 1067 Art. 75/91(B)(5) is narrower (water-supply sources only); PD 979 §3(a) excludes industrial/manufacturing effluents, so it cannot anchor this code.

links.rationale: §27(e) makes trading of wildlife unlawful and §28 scales the penalty by the species' threat category; §5(t) defines trade to include purchase, sale, export and import.
links.note: §27(f) collecting/possessing and §27(i) transporting are usually charged with (e). Inside protected areas RA 11038 §20(a)-(b) applies; RA 10654 §102 covers aquatic CITES species.

links.rationale: §99 is the most specific national provision for mangrove conversion.
links.note: PD 705 reaches only mangrove classified as forest land. For Palawan, PCSD rules under RA 7611 §19(8) apply in addition.

links.rationale: §43 bars clear-cutting of mangrove swamps set aside for coast protection and §69 penalises destruction of forest land; §3(o) defines mangrove as a forest type.
links.note: §69 is the penal hook ('destroys such forest land'). §43 is a protection/alienation restraint on shoreline mangrove strips and carries no penalty - citing it as an offence would be attacked. RA 10654 §99 is the primary provision.

links.rationale: §4(a) prohibits discharging oil or harmful substances from vessels or man-made structures at sea; §7 is the penalty.
links.note: §4(a) covers vessel/platform discharge of oil, noxious and harmful substances - not marine pollution generally (§4(b) refuse, §4(c) bank deposits). §7's penalty is displaced for §4 violations by RA 9275 §28 (₱50,000-₱1,000,000 / 1-6 years). Non-oil marine pollution fits RA 9275 §27(e) better.

remove_links.reason: Rejected by review: RA 7611 is Palawan-only and even there is a framework statute, not the offence-creating law. It has no penal section; penalties come only from PCSD rules under §19(8).
